SLC pixels are unchanged by this operator. The check is the state vectors. The desktop Apply Orbit File run is still the coordinator's. This revision applies a local EOF to the Source DIMAP or SAFE, leaves the other date in place, and writes a BEAM-DIMAP whose orbit state vectors come from that file.

Reramp multiplies by the secondary deramp/demod phase at the source coordinate. The reference burst index selects which overlap copy is read. No phase was fitted.

stages.unit_correction: An earlier status stored snap12_block_shifts_s and snap12_applied_azimuth_shift_s and described -0.001511 as seconds (about 0.735 lines). That unit was wrong. The SNAP block file and the applied value are pixels. -0.001511 px is about 3.1 microseconds. The keys are now snap12_block_shifts_px and snap12_applied_azimuth_shift_px.

stages.first_block_divergence: The file is not the amplitude-weighted double-difference tone. On the valid overlap (rows 7394:7521 and 7560:7687) that tone is -0.001477 px on SNAP pixels and -0.001588 px in this build for block 2, against the file value -0.000727 px. Replaying SpectralDiversityOp on those SNAP pixels does reproduce the file.
stages.snap_block_file_construction: The azimuth_shift.txt row is the raw per-block Periodogram in pixels. Phase is arg((master_early·conj(slave_early))·conj(master_late·conj(slave_late))). Weight is Inv Quadratic: sqrt(5x5 coherence) of the early interferogram when coherence > 0.3, else 0. The 0.3 gate is that per-pixel weight. It is not a double-difference coherence gate and it was not changed. Spectral separation is kt(range)·(linesPerBurst-overlapLines)·dt, read at column blockIndex·blockWidth (sample 0 of the swath, not the first valid sample). kt uses the first FM polynomial because the split product indexes the uncut FM list by the raster burst. The line after the block row, Mean azimuth shift, is the negated mean of blockShift·meanWeight. On the SNAP 12 back-geocoded overlap this reconstruction matches all 10 file values with maximum absolute difference 3.3e-7 px, and the applied value -0.001511319 px against the file -0.001511316 px.
stages.overlap_secondary_residual: On lines 7394:7521 and 7560:7687, block 2 columns 5109:7140, the master matches SNAP with max abs 0. The secondary amplitude relative median is 0.00325. Early-look phase residual median is -0.00129 rad, late-look +0.00190 rad. Bright pixels stay within a few milliradians. About 1.6 percent of the early-look coherence mask has a double-difference phase residual above 0.05 rad, and those pixels are the low-amplitude ones (SNAP amplitude median about 8 versus about 80 on the rest). The periodogram uses a unit phasor, so that tail moves block 2 from the file value -0.000727 px to -0.000497 px. A uniform sub-pixel shift of the SNAP secondary does not reproduce that value. Solving every pixel instead of a strided map does not remove the tail. Replacing the per-pixel range-Doppler lookup with linear interpolation between DEM posts, which is the shape of SNAP's triangle grid, moves block 2 to -0.000630 px and was not adopted.
